text.p: Yesterday's break below key support at 2.4360 marks sets sterling up for a near-term corrective move up, but it is still vulnerable to the downside with a tip lower targeting 2.4160-40, analysts said.
"Such was the scale of the decline (around two pfennigs on Tuesday) that the bounce off trendline support around 2.4260-80 was no surpise this morning," said one London based technical analyst.
Upside target of 2.4415 marks being tested and beyond lies 2.4430 and 2.4475. At 0903 GMT, the pound was trading at 2.4415/20 compared with Tuesday's 2.4300/05.
Cable powered ahead through resistance at $1.6145 amid talk of buying out of Asia, possibly by the People's Bank of China.
Next major resistance is pegged at $1.6200 with a much stronger ceiling at $1.6245.
Sterling's correction from the $1.6040 high reached on Monday was limited by support at the lower trendline channel around $1.6040 so the uptrend channel is intact, analysts said.
Minor resistance at $1.6160 has broken setting up a test to to the upper boundary of the major ascending channel around $1.6205, technical analysts said.
